newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria civil servants threaten strike over cuts.
newsitem.headline: Austria civil servants threaten strike over cuts.

text.p: Austrian civil servants, police officials and university teachers agreed on Monday to stage their first strike in seven years if the government fails to act on their grievances over cost-cutting.
Public Service Union (GOeD) head Siegfried Dohr announced the unanimous decision at the end of a meeting of the union's executive committee.
He accused the government of delaying tactics and warned action could start in days if the situation did not improve.
"We will not allow ourselves to be fobbed off by the government any longer," Dohr told reporters.
The threatened strike would be the first by public sector workers since a 24-hour protest in 1990 and would sully the nation's otherwise harmonious record of industrial relations.
Civil servants, protected from redundancy by law, rarely flex their muscles but in recent months they have become increasingly unhappy at government cost-cutting.
They say staff numbers have been reduced and pay packets eroded by cuts aimed at ensuring Austria qualifies for a single European currency.
"The government will only give way if we exert pressure," said Wolfgang Pertmayr, representative of civil servants within the finance ministry.
Civil servants in the finance and environment ministries say they have borne the brunt of cuts, with the loss of around 1,000 posts in recent years and plans to scrap another 700 by the year 2000.
Teachers are disgruntled over proposals to reduce the number of university places while civil servants in the police force say they are understaffed.
Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary in the finance ministry, said he had "taken note" of the union's decision but he urged employees to show restraint.
"It would be more sensible to seek a common solution and negotiate," Ruttenstorfer said.
"But the government has a duty to its tax payers to use their money wisely. That is why the public sector must become more efficient and keep pace with private industry," he added.
A fresh round of talks with university teachers was due on Monday evening. The unions said they would be watching for signs the government was taking the strike threat seriously.
The ultimatum comes days before government and public sector employees begin negotiating next year's pay deal.
Many civil servants received no increase this year as part of the government's austerity drive.
"As far as we are concerned there is no question of another zero pay increase," Dohr said.
